outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Cybersecurity & enterprise software, led by CrowdStrike, Zscaler, ServiceNow and Salesforce
strongest.reason: the AI-safety debate hardened into a full sector rotation today, with CrowdStrike and Zscaler both surging double digits as Microsoft's new AI safety framework reinforced the narrative that rising AI risk is a tailwind for security and platform spending

strongest.area: Humanoid robotics, led by UBTECH Robotics
strongest.reason: shares jumped after the company was approved to lead two new national humanoid-robot technical standards and closed a roughly HK$24.1B share placement, the largest ever for a listed humanoid-robot company, a sharp reversal from Monday's decline

weakest.area: Chips, chip equipment & AI compute, led by ASML, Teradyne, Arm, AMD and Micron
weakest.reason: the AI-pacing selloff broadened today beyond memory names into logic, IP and fab-equipment names, with chip-equipment peers Applied Materials and Lam Research also falling sharply as investors reassess AI capex assumptions

weakest.area: Macro backdrop, with the 10-year yield near 5% and oil above $100
weakest.reason: cross-asset caution is building into Wednesday's FOMC decision, where markets are split between a hold and a hike after Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, while oil remains elevated on Middle East supply risk

outlook.nextStep: Two macro catalysts dominate this week: the Senate's CLARITY Act procedural vote today, which is pressuring crypto as it nears, and Wednesday's 2pm ET FOMC decision, with markets roughly split between a hold and a quarter-point hike. The chip and chip-equipment selloff broadening beyond memory into logic and fab-tool names is worth close attention for whether hyperscaler capex commentary this week confirms or reverses the repricing. The cybersecurity/enterprise-software rotation and today's UBTECH strength look like the more constructive stories right now, but given how fast both moved in a single session, they're probably better watched for durability over the next few sessions than chased immediately.

signals.title: AI-pacing selloff broadens beyond memory into logic and chip-equipment names
signals.body: Following Dario Amodei's weekend essay urging AI developers to slow the pace of frontier model development, Monday's selloff (concentrated in memory names) spread further on Tuesday: Intel dropped roughly 7%, AMD sank about 6%, and chip-equipment makers Applied Materials, Lam Research and ASML all fell sharply as the pacing call reached fab-spending assumptions. Notably, Amodei explicitly ruled out halting AI training, and Anthropic itself disclosed a partnership to deploy AMD's MI450 GPUs.
signals.focus: the selloff broadening beyond its original memory-chip epicenter is worth close attention for whether it's a one-time repricing or the start of a more sustained AI-capex reassessment

signals.title: Cybersecurity rally intensifies as Microsoft's AI safety framework adds fuel
signals.body: CrowdStrike surged roughly 14% and Zscaler jumped over 16%, with Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet, Rubrik and Qualys also participating, as Microsoft's newly announced AI safety framework reinforced the view that rising AI risk translates into a new, durable enterprise-security spending category (agent identity, runtime security, monitoring, access controls).
signals.focus: a continuing trend worth tracking, though the scale of today's move is unusually large and durability over the next few sessions is the real test

signals.title: FOMC decision Wednesday at 2pm ET with markets split on a hike
signals.body: The Fed's rate decision lands Wednesday, September 16 at 2pm ET, with the target range currently at 3.50%-3.75%. Markets have been pricing a quarter-point hike to 3.75%-4.00% as slightly more likely than not following Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech and a solid August jobs report, though cooling CPI (down to 3.4% in July) and softer retail-sales data keep a hold scenario very much in play.
signals.focus: the week's biggest single catalyst; probably better watched than traded ahead of tomorrow's decision given how split the market is

signals.title: CLARITY Act Senate vote today pressures crypto off overnight highs
signals.body: Bitcoin pulled back to around $77,000-$77,800, giving back roughly 3% from an overnight high above $79,500, as the Senate prepares a procedural vote today on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, which needs 60 votes to advance and would divide crypto oversight between the SEC and CFTC. Democrats are still seeking changes despite reported White House agreement on revised ethics language, and NY AG Letitia James is leading 18 state AGs in opposition.
signals.focus: a binary-ish legislative catalyst worth monitoring closely today; the outcome of the procedural vote could move crypto meaningfully in either direction

signals.title: UBTECH Robotics reverses higher on national-standards approval and record placement
signals.body: UBTECH Robotics shares jumped after the company was approved to lead two new national humanoid-robot technical standards (positioning/navigation and human-machine interaction) and completed a roughly HK$24.1B share placement — the largest financing of its kind for a listed humanoid-robot company, exceeding its four prior placements combined.
signals.focus: a sharp reversal from Monday's decline worth watching for follow-through, particularly given the scale of the new capital raise

signals.title: Teradyne among the hardest hit as chip-equipment selloff deepens
signals.body: Teradyne shares tumbled roughly 13%, among the session's worst performers as the broader semiconductor-equipment sector sold off alongside the AI-pacing call reaching fab-spending names, compounded by profit-taking after a recent run and news of a new support office opening in Bengaluru.
signals.focus: the sharpest single-day move in the tracker; worth watching closely for whether it extends or partially reverses once full-session volume comes in

signals.title: Oil holds above $100, tracking closely with the rise in Treasury yields
signals.body: WTI crude remains elevated above $100 a barrel, with commentary today highlighting the tightening correlation between oil, Treasury yields and equities as markets weigh both the ongoing Middle East supply risk and tomorrow's Fed decision.
signals.focus: worth monitoring for follow-through, especially given the added inflation-pressure angle heading into the Fed meeting
